description:
AUDITED at origin/main `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83` (2026-09-02).

## Status

LIVE. `TypeExpr::Map` parses and resolves, but the quoted `@spec` fragment splitter does not count its opening token. This breaks every boundary that must occur after a map; a map at the final EOF-delimited position may succeed accidentally.

## Exact behavior

```fz
@spec g(%{b: integer}) :: any
fn g(m), do: m
fn main(), do: dbg(g(%{b: 2}))
```

`fz2 interp` exits 1:

```text
error[parse/expected-token]: expected `)` after @spec param list, got eof
  --> ...:1:27
```

The same failure occurs with `@spec g(%{b: integer}, integer) :: any`.

Affected sibling boundaries:

```fz
@spec %{b: integer} + integer :: any
@spec integer + %{b: integer} :: any
@spec g(t) :: %{b: integer} when t: integer
@spec g(t, u) :: any when t: %{b: integer}, u: integer
```

Controls:

```fz
@spec g(any) :: %{b: integer}
@spec g(t) :: any when t: %{b: integer}
@spec g({integer, integer}) :: any
@spec g(%P{}) :: any
```

The first two controls succeed only because the map ends at EOF; tuple and struct forms succeed normally. Elixir 1.19.4 accepts a map type in parameter position.

## Root cause

`FragmentCursor::collect_type_tokens` in `src/compiler2/quoted_function.rs` increments depth for `LParen | LBrack | LBrace`, but the lexer emits `%{` as the single token `Tok::PercentLBrace`. Its closing `RBrace` therefore changes depth from 0 to -1. `TypeTokenBoundary::stops_before` refuses every boundary while depth is nonzero, so the collector consumes the delimiter and remaining payload.

The resulting diagnostic depends on the boundary: parameter and infix forms run to EOF; a return before `when` leaves `When` inside the type expression; a nonfinal constraint leaves `Comma` and the next constraint inside it.

## Required fix

Treat `Tok::PercentLBrace` as an opening delimiter in `collect_type_tokens`. Prefer one local delimiter-depth classifier shared by the fragment-depth scans so paired-token knowledge cannot drift. Do not special-case an individual `TypeTokenBoundary`.

## Tests / acceptance

1. Add focused quoted-function surface tests proving map types split correctly at every affected boundary: named spec parameter before `)` and before `,`; infix spec left/right operands; result type before `when`; constraint before `,`.
2. Keep EOF-final return and constraint map forms green, but do not use them as the red regression.
3. Keep tuple and `%P{}` controls green.
4. Add/run an end-to-end map-parameter spec program and require `%{:b => 2}` on the supported execution lanes.
5. Run focused tests, formatting, clippy with warnings denied, `cargo test --lib`, and the fixture matrix.

`cargo test --locked --lib compiler2::type_expr_test` passes all 18 tests at the audited commit, confirming the map grammar itself is healthy; existing coverage does not exercise the quoted-`@spec` fragment boundaries.
title: [BUG] @spec fragment boundaries lose `%{...}` map types because `PercentLBrace` does not open delimiter depth
